gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-imperial: Noto Sans Imperial Aramaic reads friendly and straightforward, its c ending in two open pincer tips and capitals barely rising above the lowercase. Origami's brush-drawn heading stands apart from it.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-inscript: Origami paints its letters like a sign-painter, one unshaded stroke with no tilt in the rounds. Noto Sans Inscriptional Parthian follows in plain sans form, with wide-eyed e and a shapes and a deep middle band, and it holds up at larger body sizes.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-jp: Noto Sans JP stands tall, its x-height high and its curves sweeping open. Origami's neon-tube lettering takes the heading, so the body can stay quiet beneath it.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-kaithi: Poured lead meets painted signage here. Origami's gentle monotone strokes carry the heading, while Noto Sans Kaithi fills each line with lowercase that nearly matches its capitals, keeping the text sturdy under the brushwork.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-kannada: Noto Sans Kannada lets its s curves open wide at both ends, with a gentle step up to the capitals. And Origami, whose t has a crossbar as thick as its stem, is the one built to make a statement.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-kayah-li: Origami draws every glyph with an unmodulated line, like a single pass of a sign-painter's brush. And Noto Sans Kayah Li lifts its brush ends before curves close, which is what makes the two feel related.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-kharosht: Noto Sans Kharoshthi lays down a thick, dark stripe of lowercase, its curves never closing back on themselves. Origami, with no vertical emphasis and no thinning across its strokes, sits above it as a bold painted counterpart.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-khmer: Contemporary and a little unusual, Origami holds its line thickness steady like a brush pulled once. Noto Sans Khmer does the quieter work, with generous openings and small letters standing nearly as proud as capitals.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-khojki: Modern in feel, Noto Sans Khojki gives every e a large clear eye and exits wide enough to pass light through, beneath Origami's fat-crossbar heading. Paragraphs would stay open and easy going.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-khudawad: Noto Sans Khudawadi keeps capitals close to lowercase height and leaves its rounds unsealed, like an unlatched hook, under Origami's heading. Origami's zero stroke contrast is the strongest quality here.
